title: Novametrics POC weekly sync — batching vs caching economics
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review latest pilot economics. Key focus: tokens/sec/$ ratios across model variants, observed caching savings from prefix/KV cache, and tradeoffs when increasing batch sizes (latency p50 vs p95). Agreed next steps include running a 48-hour end-to-end benchmark with production prompts and sharing adjusted batching config. Action items assigned for benchmarks, security docs, and pricing calibration.
next_steps: Redwood to run 48h e2e benchmark with production prompt set and share results (Jordan)
Novametrics to provide 10k sample production prompts and traffic profile (Alec)
SE to share suggested batching + cache config JSON and kernel/profile notes (Samira)
Pricing and pilot extension proposal from Jordan by 2026-08-24

Samira Huang: upload batching+cache config + notes to shared drive — due 2026-08-21

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM); Alec, Priya, Markus, Tanya (Novametrics)

[00:00:00] Jordan: ok thanks everyone for joining, uh quick note we only have 45 minutes so we'll go through the numbers quickly and then decisions.
[00:00:12] Alec: sounds good, excited to see the cache numbers we looked at the dashboard this morning but want more detail.
[00:00:20] Samira: cool, I'll start with the brief recap on what we changed since last week — we bumped per-shard batch size from 8 to 16 and turned on prefix/KV caching for the longest common prefix in your prompt set. We also tested int8 quantization on the 13B variant.
[00:00:38] Priya: and we saw some cost drops, but latency spikes at peak, that's our worry.
[00:00:45] Samira: right. Quick numbers: baseline (no cache, batch=8, fp16) — ~950 tokens/sec per GPU and cost ~= $0.0024 per token equivalent (that's tokens per dollar inverted) — when we enabled prefix KV cache hit ~44% after warmup and tokens/sec effectively rose to ~1,600 for cache hits; effective tokens/sec/$ improved by ~1.6x overall.
[00:01:10] Markus: those are overall numbers but what's the p95? p50? we care about tail.
[00:01:16] Samira: p50 latency around 85ms for batch=8 fp16, p95 about 320ms. After batching to 16 p50 improves to 72ms but p95 climbs to 420ms during concurrent spikes — so we trade higher throughput for worse tail latency.
[00:01:34] Alec: ok that matches what we feared. Our product team needs p95 < 400ms for interactive flows.
[00:01:40] Jordan: quick interrupt — is that p95 measured at app-layer or runtime-level? meaning including network and prefix cache lookup time?
[00:01:47] Samira: good q — these numbers are runtime-only, model + kernel time. We added a 15-20ms avg overhead in pipeline to account for network/RPC in our estimate.
[00:01:58] Tanya: so if we add 20ms that pushes p95 over the product SLO in some slots. Any levers?
[00:02:04] Samira: yes — two main levers: reduce batch size back to 8 and rely more on cache or use hybrid batch sizing (adaptive batching) so under low qps we keep small batches, under high qps we increase. Second lever is to pin a smaller model variant for interactive route (6B int8) for strict latency.
[00:02:20] Priya: curious about cache warmup time — your dashboard showed hit rate jumped after 40 minutes. Is that expected?
[00:02:25] Samira: yes your workload has a lot of repeated prefixes (search templates) so the KV cache warms to ~40% hit in 30-45 minutes in steady traffic. Cold starts are expensive though. We've got options: pre-warm the cache by replaying sample traffic during deploy window — that's what we recommended for the pilot.
[00:02:42] Alec: conversation drift means we won't get that steady-state always. We have a lot of tail queries and some one-offs. Cache won't help those. How much does batching hurt those one-offs?
[00:02:51] Samira: one-offs do not benefit from KV prefix cache; batching helps amortize per-request overhead but introduces wait time. At low concurrency, batching has minimal wait (we use a latency-aware batching window of 20ms), but at mid concurrency you start seeing 50-150ms added per request if you buffer to fill batch.
[00:03:10] Markus: can you show us the tokens/sec/$ delta when combining int8 quant + cache + batch16?
[00:03:14] Samira: sure — combined (int8, batch=16, cached prefixes) we measured ~2,500 tokens/sec per GPU on cache hits, effective tokens per dollar improved ~2.8x versus baseline. But again that baseline had better p95. So cost wins but worst-case latency increases.
[00:03:30] Jordan: and have we tried dynamic fallback? like default to 6B int8 for interactive endpoints and use 13B fp16 for higher-compute background routes?
[00:03:38] Samira: yes that's a common pattern — route by intent/label. Redwood supports automatic routing by policy; you can pin model variants per route. We can demo policy rules in the console.
[00:03:48] Alec: latency-sensitive chat must hit p95 < 400ms — so maybe route to 6B int8 with caching for common prompts and use 13B as a fallback for high-quality long generations.
[00:03:58] Priya: how does quantization affect output quality? we've had hallucination sensitivity in our tests.
[00:04:03] Samira: int8 tends to be fine for short completions, we ran evals on your prompt set: ROUGE and task accuracy drop was within 1-2% for most prompts, but there are edge cases where answer specificity degrades. We should run focused evals on your high-risk prompts.
[00:04:18] Tanya: that'd be helpful — we have a list of 120 critical prompts.
[00:04:21] Samira: great, send them and we'll run a focused regression set.
[00:04:25] Luis: on the ops side, one more thing — caching KV memory footprint scales with your unique prefix count; Priya, you'll need to plan GPU memory if you want large cache windows.
[00:04:34] Priya: noted. what's the memory per key roughly?
[00:04:36] Samira: depends on model context size; ballpark 1.2-1.8MB per active key for your 2k token contexts. So 10k prefixes ~12-18GB.
[00:04:50] Alec: ouch that's non-trivial for on-prem. We might need to tune window size.
[00:04:54] Samira: yep — TTL eviction, LRU, and sharding strategies help. Also you can cache only top-k prefixes.
[00:05:02] Markus: regarding billing — can we get token-level cost attribution per route so our product team can see exact tokens/sec/$ for interactive vs background?
[00:05:09] Jordan: yes Redwood Console supports per-route cost breakdown — we'll enable route tags for your pilot and share a demo.
[00:05:16] Alec: perfect. can you also give us a delta if we switch to dedicated capacity? we're on hosted now.
[00:05:22] Jordan: dedicated cost model reduces per-token by about 20-35% depending on commit level; important to model utilization. If you get to >60% utilization steady, dedicated gets cheaper.
[00:05:32] Priya: our utilization is spiky so not sure. we might do hybrid: hosted for dev and dedicated for steady nightly batch jobs.
[00:05:38] Samira: that's a valid pattern. Also note dedicated gives you more control over kernel selection and GPU type which can improve throughput further.
[00:05:46] Alec: ok for immediate next step we want Redwood to run a 48-hour e2e benchmark with our 10k prompts including bursts to model production. What's the plan?
[00:05:55] Jordan: we'll run the benchmark on your data set (anonymized), include both batch configs and cache-enabled runs, and return a spreadsheet with tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, p50/p95/p99 latencies and cache hit curves. Samira will configure runs.
[00:06:09] Samira: yes we'll do 4 runs: baseline, cache-only, batch-hybrid, int8+cache+batch. We'll also capture CPU/GPU utilization and memory.
[00:06:18] Priya: can we have the test run from our VPC? we need to validate network egress and peering.
[00:06:23] Jordan: yes Priya — we'll coordinate VPC peering window. Expect small performance delta from hosted vs peered due to network RTT but we'll measure it.
[00:06:31] Markus: about security, we've asked for SOC2 docs and KMS support last week, any update?
[00:06:36] Jordan: I sent SOC2 link earlier but will re-share; Redwood supports KMS integrations and you can control key rotation. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[00:06:44] Alec: great. two more quick Qs — does Redwood report tokenization mismatch? some of our telemetry counts token differently causing accounting mismatch.
[00:06:52] Samira: yes we have a tokenization mapping utility and we'll sync token counts; sometimes libraries differ by 1-2% if you use byte-pair vs internal tokenizer. We'll include mapping script.
[00:07:02] Tanya: final: can you brief on rollback policies if a model quality regression happens in production?
[00:07:07] Samira: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous pinned model; you can configure auto-detect quality regressions from your eval set and trigger rollback. We can demo the rollback flow.
[00:07:18] Jordan: ok wrapping up — quick recap of action items and dates (see shared notes). Any objections?
[00:07:24] Alec: none, just want the benchmark asap.
[00:07:26] Markus: no objections.
[00:07:28] Priya: thanks everyone.
[00:07:30] Jordan: thanks all, will follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark window and share pricing doc. Bye.
[00:07:36] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: speaker labels may be imperfect; occasional filler words left in. Some numeric values rounded for readability.
